The class keeps you busy with multiple assignments but so do other ME 3345 sections. I really don't get the other comments that speak ill of Dr. Menon. Don't hate the player hate the game.

Most of the heat transfer professors at Tech are terrible, Professor Menon is still difficult (it's a difficult class), but is an incredible professor. Probably my favorite teacher this year; knows what he's talking about too, so not just a set of jokes in a trench coat but actual good educator. Wish he could teach the rest of my sysarch classes.

Even without being a professor and teaching for one semester, he is the best you can get at GT: Easily understood lectures, numerous metaphors for concepts making them easy to grasp. As long as you attend lecture (they are a good time), you will get an A. He is just that good. More professors need to look towards how he teaches o7

The best thing about him was he didn't read of the powerpoint and made us understand the lecture but one thing is he writes most of the stuff on white board so if you sit really back you probably wouldn't see it clearly but overall still the best one I have had at tech
Great teacher. Clearly passionate on what he is teaching. He explained everything really well and did a great job of creating connection between the class and real world applications.

Got put on the spot to teach 2110 and did an amazing job with it. Super funny guy and very knowledgeable about the content, he had no problem answering any question thrown his way even if it was out of the scope of the class. Extremely dismissive and cold. Idk she's a good professor but a bit overstimulating for me. I get it she asks us questions in lecture frequently to get us to reinforce and connect the knowledge we know but she does it in condescending way when someone doesn't know an answer. She's blunt and funny and gives good advice though.

analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class is rewarding, although difficult. The material is basically just learning how to program a GBA in C. Tests are quite difficult and graded harshly. HW5 is not for the faint of heart. The end of semester project is fun but lots of requirements, so will take up a good bit of time. For the love of god attend lecture, itll help on the HWs

Amazing Course, but extremely brutial for those not used to mini projects. I think this is the introduction to longer homeworks for those in CS or CM, but as a CmpE it kinda helps you with working on lengthly assignments. Tests are hit or miss, but if you come to class you'll be fine. Start on the final project early to create something good.

Professor Hansen is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is super passionate about this class and the topic is very interesting. Expect a lot of hw and labs! The tests are very hard and some might even consider harder than CS2110. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! Aaron is very good and caring prof. but the materials are better taught 1v1 than in class

The best class i've ever taken, that being said, get ready to WORK. Hansen's a great lecturer and clearly passionate but the nature of the course is super difficult. At least 5 hrs a week in the first 2 months and 10-15+ after that. He's very accessible and kind to all students, but the TAs carry the course. Go to office hours and recitation!!

The HW took up my wkends and especially the last ones had me (and the whole class) going crazy. Aaron is passionate about this topic, & I respect him. The TAs are FANTASTIC and work their heads off helping and explaining every important detail to us. I wonder sometimes if 2110 would have been less stressful...The final project is fulfilling though.

analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: His lectures are mandatory and more like a review than actual teaching. Exams are only 2 questions, best practice is the review he gives before. He grades in one sitting and basically only checks final answers, so any mistake will ruin your score. The course itself isn't too bad; it's a time sucker, but you can just learn from videos online.

One of my favorite professors yet. Very serious about teaching, to the point that you shouldn't expect him to let you sit in class all day texting or scrolling. That being said, he has an amazing way of explaining every topic and proves pretty much everything that he puts in the notes. Also, he lets you know what he expects on each exam beforehand.

Mr. Yavari is very passionate about teaching and genuinely cares about his students. If you need to miss an exam for a valid reason, he'll work with you on finding a time to take it as long as you give him enough notice. He's a bit of a harsh grader on exams but generally exams are quite simple and nearly the same as the practice exams.

He is a great professor! I was initially unsure but quickly realized that I got lucky being in his class. He truly cares about teaching and wants you to really understand the material, which is more than most professors can say. He is lenient and very fair on exams because he teaches the material thoroughly. I can't recommend him enough!

Was initially scared reading past reviews—they are mostly untrue. He's not mean and he's actually really funny in class. Though his lectures are hard to understand, he posts lecture notes on Canvas so you can review them later. His tests are similar to practice exams, and if you read the textbook/go to class, the homework is not hard either.

Dr. Buskell is an absolute gem. He's caring, passionate about teaching, clear on expectations, and just a great guy to be around. I honestly don't understand all the bad reviews. He is a nice professor and does a good job teaching concepts. Most students tend to just blame the professor whenever they struggle lol. Go to class, ask questions, and practice and you will be good. HWs are long and suck though.

Biggest troll I have encountered in my ed career. Copies slides from textbook & codes demos super fast. Instead of lecture read his slides, do slide practices & read textbook if stuck. TAs are amazing for HW help & explaining concepts. Start HW early. Teaches surface level of content to have time to ask riddles & gets mad if you know the answer.

Lectures weren't paced great - introductions to concepts went too slow and coding examples went too fast to retain anything. I personally struggled going in unfamiliar with java. This class has been the worst class I have ever taken. analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 158 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Alicea is by far the best professor for Physics. For those who say her exams are hard and beyond what they believe was taught, you're wrong. As long as you understand the content well and its applications, no matter the question given, you'll be able to apply what you know. Not to mention the generous partial credit given. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!!!

She is an outstanding professor. I took this class online and found it much easier than the in-person version. The recorded lectures explain the concepts very clearly, and the ample practice tests prepared me well for exams. As long as you pay attention to the recorded lectures and utilize the GPS and practice tests, this class is a breeze.

The lecturer does a great job at giving you ample amounts of practice material, relevant examples through labs and group-work problems over teams, and has access to many helpful TA's while being very responsive to emails and questions on Ed-Stem. Tests are hard, with self-studying being necessary to pass. Hard class, good teacher.
Best professor for physics 2. Took this course online and it was easy.

Dr. Alicea is by far the best Physics Prof at Tech. She takes complicated information and presents it in an easy-to-understand way with TONS of examples. Physics II is a challenging course, and the tests reflect that. However, the grade breakdown allows you to succeed even if you don't do very well on the three midterms and final.

analysis.name: Amelia Stokolosa
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Such a kind and relatable person. She does a wonderful job explaining and going into depth about the content in class. She does talk and go very fast so be prepared. I loved how she would always try and get the class involved during lecture. I always look forward to going to her class. Don't skip lecture and do the practice!

The class is pretty engaging overall, and she genuinely cares about her students. Best class this semester!! I used to look forward to class every week, because yes, it is THAT fun. Would take her again 100% . The exams can be challenging at first, but it's all centralized across all 1553 sections.

Overall super engaging class, she goes a little fast sometimes but takes on the somewhat complex topics in an approachable and clear way. Do not recommend skipping any lectures though as a lot of the concepts pile up on each other quickly, especially towards the end of the semester.
A professor who does her job well and there is really nothing to be worried about when taking a class with her.
Sometimes goes a tiny bit fast but other than that, she is slay and had us learn a tiny bit of French for funsies. Some classes made me laugh out loud

review_highlights.comment: Expects students to have 20hrs/week set aside for this class. During exams, it was common to see people crying. The problems were unlike those we went over and were impossible to complete in the given time. Studied for the final for a week, 14hrs/day, and could not complete half of it. HW graded harshly and barely any review material. Ok to reach.

Avoid at all costs. He's a nice guy and cares a lot but his expectations are way to high. Teaches purely conceptual in class and then expects you to learn everything on the homework, which is impossible without a software that he doesn't teach you how to use. Class is 20+ hours of work per week. Tests are abysmal and good luck finishing in time.

Only section that didn't have a take home final, and got the lowest avg on the 2nd exam. The hw's are long, and graded harshly and the lectures are conceptual. I helped other sections study for their finals and their review question were far easier. We got only two review questions per test. Hardest tests I've taken at GT. Caring guy.

A very challenging class however you learn a lot because of it. Be ready to delve deep and truly learn the subject and do the work to get to that point! Dr. El Fil despite the grading cares for the students and by going to office hours and taking some time the course and his lectures are really enjoyable!

This class was by far the most work I have ever done. The homework in this class would take around 12 hours per week, and that is not an overestimate. On the final, there were things that we had never seen before. Teaching-wise, a limited amount of foundational concepts were covered, and you were just thrown into the fire to figure it out.

analysis.name: Sven Behrens
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: My only complaint about Behrens is that I think he forgets what it's like to not have multiple physics degrees; really hard class overall. He's so so nice and really cares about his students. He will drop everything to help you, super accommodating, cares about student feedback. Go to office hours, they're amazing. Brought donuts to the final

Behrens is such a great professor and person. Took Phys2231 with him, and while it was an incredibly challenging class he worked hard to make sure every one of us succeeded. Put in the work to the class and he will put in the work to help you. Such a funny, earnest guy who really does care about his teaching. Got a 76 in class but rounded to a B.

The lectures were quite content-heavy, and overall I felt they mostly were tangential, focusing quite a lot on finding derivations instead of practicing concepts. He was quite accessible outside of class and very friendly and helpful to students.

He did a very good job of teaching the material and explained concepts well with good practice problems. Also is super funny and genuinely one of the most caring professors. Really wants his sections to succeeds, is super available outside of class, and frequently asks for and applies any feedback given very happily. Would definitely recommend.

I struggled significantly in this course, but that was no fault of his. Honestly, I believe I may not have even had the chance at passing this course without him. Dr. Behrens is very kind and considerate of his students. He goes above & beyond to help his students succeed. If you have to take this course, he is by far the best professor.

He's a good lecturer, and the thought this class is a bit of an out of order way, awkward but manageable, he's very cool and nice, sometimes I wish the tests weren't so coherent at times and the curve in the class was a bit akward, nonetheless if he was to teach the class I would take it, just make sure you pay attention.

Professor Blough's lectures are clear and informative. The tests are reasonable, and if you watch the lectures and do the homework assignments, you can definitely do well on the exams. I did not like the use of HonorLock, but other than that this class was great and very interesting.

His lecture by itself is pretty clear but homework and tests are miles harder than materials on lecture. You can't just attend lectures and do homework to expect good grade. You have to read and study on your own. Expect to read every single section of the textbook to pass this 3 hour course. He's helpful during office hour though.

Very informative, understanding, and fair. The organization of his class is very well structured and makes online class a lot easier to handle. The homeworks are fair. Start early. The mesh subdivision homework is the hardest. For the tests, study the test review. I highly recommend him as a professor.

amazing professor, clearly deeply knowledgable about computer graphics but also radiates a passion for the field that is truly contagious and inspiring. the course is what you want to make of it, the assignments are filling in blanks and easily cheesable, quizzes are open note, so if you want a stronger foundation in the theory it'll be up to you

Prof. Zhu is a great lecturer who does a really good job of breaking down difficult concepts. He's clearly passionate about what he teaches, which makes lectures enjoyable, and he also offers Zoom options and recordings. The class is well structured with eight projects, a final project, and two online, open-note tests. I recommend taking his class.

This class has 8 super easy hws, 2 medium-difficult quizzes (depending on whether you studied hard or not), and a final project. I expected this class to be difficult or take a lot of my time, but it was honestly so chill. The instructions for the hws are very straight-forward and clear, and I never got stuck at all. Bho Zhu loves what he teaches.

Dr. Zhu is a goated professor. There are 8 straightforward programming assignments, 2 open-note take-home online quizzes, and the class overall is great. He's super knowledgeable and clearly knows his stuff, if you can take him for graphics, 100% do it

analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Overall, this class isn't very difficult in terms of content. You typically have one or two writing assignments due every week that just ask you to reflect on what you discussed in lecture or an external website. Attendance is mandatory, but slides are uploaded to Canvas; most people do other work during lecture since there is no midterm/final.

The class is super chill and is an easy a if you do assignments. She's a chill lecturer and cares about the material and her students. The new group project was interesting, but I'm sure she'll improve it for future semesters. Great professor if you want a stress-free class

Took this course asynchronously. We had a lecture and a few assignments posted each week. The lectures were quite engaging and required little work. Class focused on dimensions of wellness and helped me learn a lot of strategies to improve each! Overall, great class with a great professor and TAs who are always willing to help.

If you are just looking to get the required health credit done take this course! Mandatory attendance at lectures will take up about 2 hours, and then there's only like 2 hours of busy work a week. No tests, no quizzes, no long essays. Very nice professor, and lectures are interesting if you do decide to pay attention

Professor Baradel is amazing! All you had to do was complete the homework (generally very quick and easy, not graded harshly at all) and show up to class (she gives like 4 free absences though). She is super sweet and accommodating with assignments, too!

analysis.name: Abrahim Ladha
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 181 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I think Ladha is a chill guy. However, it's pretty clear that the expectations of the course don't really align with the reality. I don't think the exams are fairly written and there should be, at the very least, an exam drop for this class (like other CS2050). The TAs need less power though; they practically run the course and not in a good way.

Take if you are 100% sure that you will attend all lectures + solve all homework + all practice problems + spend a lot of time trying to combine your knowledge from the lectures with the extremely difficult practice problems, and expect even more "creative", harder questions to appear on your exam. You need to practice as if this is your only class

Why is this called an intro class. Homeworks take min 6 hrs a week, TAs cant help much, it's too hard. Test reviews are so useless from TAs. If you get a C on 1 exam, no chance of an A.

He's a nice guy, content itself isn't even really that bad, but the class structure is absolutely abysmal. Save yourself the headache and transfer in the credit.

Ladha himself is a good lecturer and a good person. It's his TA's that make the class a nightmare. Just because they went through hell in their semester they think it's their turn to give us hell back. HW's took 6+ hrs per week and exams had singular questions worth 5+% of your COURSE GRADE. Absolutely do not take this class under any circumstances

This class actively regressed my knowledge of discrete mathematics and math as a whole. If God wished to give his strongest warriors a challenge, he would send students to CS2050 Office Hours to face the awful TAs for this class. Such students would emerge Navy SEALs.  Ladha is a terrible lecturer and teaches content that cater to few. Do not take.

analysis.name: Brian Beck
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Easy to get A's on labs, but the quizzes vary by section and there's no good way to study for it. You could get a 100 on a lab and a 30 on the quiz and your grade drops more than if it was in the reverse even though they're weighed the same. Good luck on getting a good TA because that matters the most.

You won't see this dude, quizzes depend on your TA. Go to class, read the manual beforehand. It's an annoying class but the TA's are helpful. You probably won't learn much from the labs but the circuits can be cool. Lab exam is fine, you'll get a study guide the week before. Just learn the book properly and YouTube the theory and you'll be fine.

He hadn't taught the class in several years, so maybe this will be a little biased, but the exams were really hard (until the final, when he deliberately made it easier). Everyone above an 89% got an A in the class. The homeworks also took a long time--they weren't graded for accuracy, but I still wanted to try and get them correct.

This class is like ECE 3043 but improved. That being said it is still a difficult class that takes a lot of time but you learn a lot more and get a lot more out of it. There were 3 tests which were fair, a final project, and a handful of labs which all took longer than the dedicated lab time. However, Dr. Beck was very supportive throughout.
If you don't get a good TA, good luck. Horrendously run class with zero room for error.

review_highlights.comment: She's not a bad teacher but uses few examples and expects you to know more than she teaches. She isn't very nice to students, especially when talking one on one. She is very unforgiving.

Rude when answering questions in class. Test grading was unfair, my first exam I got every answer but one out of 25 correct numerically and got a D. If you don't do something exactly the way she wants it done, you will get punished with the grade you get with zero flexibility. Be on your best behavior in class. She has photographic memory of all the little bad traits you show in class, but none of the good ones.

Two midterms, 9 HW's which are just writing 2 questions per HW problem, final is no longer optional. Polarizing professor for sure. Responds sarcastically to some questions, lectures fast, and is a tough grader. To offset her rough exams, she provides 5 bonus points via bonus assignments which she would often poorly explain and are due next class.

Professor Bassiri-Gharb is the best professor I've taken at Tech to be honest. She's extremely caring, understanding and reasonable. She's very straightforward on how to be successful in her class, and her exams are very fair based off of in-class examples, homeworks, and past exams. Made Thermo easier to understand and loved taking her section

Professor Chilton is easily the best professor I've had at Tech. She clearly is passionate about the subject she teaches. I took her online during the summer and she kept my attention the whole time as she is an extremely fun lecturer. Class attendance is mandatory, but you will want to come with her as a professor. Labs are extremely easy.

The professor is really lenient and understanding - the lectures are also extremely interesting. Labs can be time consuming but the lectures and coursework are relatively easy work. Honestly a 10/10 professor, she was really sweet and clearly cared about the content she teaches.

Dr. Chilton is an awesome professor. I had her along with Dr. Handlos for EAS1601 and the class was super fun. Not only is is very interesting, but the assignments were not extremely hard either. If you showed up to lecture and actually studied the materials for tests, you were fine. The labs were a little time consuming though.

Co-taught EAS 1601 with Dr. Handlos, as well as managing all the labs. Solid prof, and very caring. The labs are pretty easy if you have a good group - and a portion of it you can do online for completion credit. The lab grade can really boost your overall grade.

Great professor. Lectures are engaging and clear. He clearly cares about his students. Goes question by question when explaining what is going to be on the test. You will not regret taking his class.

Holy goat. Not particularly good at this subject and kinda fumbled on a test that cost me an A in the class, but I very much enjoyed his class. Got me a lot more interested in accounting. Not hard to lock in on this class and get an A, Professor Blunck basically gives you test blueprints. Great teacher.

He's the best!! He clearly cares about his students and tries his best to make accounting fun. He tells you every problem before the test so just review/memorize the problems from the notes and you will do fine. You don't really need to do the recommended textbook problems and he has videos on the concepts if you miss something in class.

Had this prof for MGT 4026, MGT 4029, and MGT 4043. His classes are straightforward with outlines and lectures videos you can refer back to. I wouldn't really recommend stacking his classes because he puts his exam dates on the same day for all of them.

He reminds me of Dale from Horrible Bosses. Anyways he talks really slowly, so it's best to watch lectures online at 2x speed. There's A LOT of MML homework, but he's super chill on deadlines. Dr. Mayer is such a great professor. He consistently helps his students understand even the most difficult concepts, he s extrenmely friendly, and his sample exams are very similar to his actual ones. He made me enjoy a class I never thought I would and I finished with an A so thats always a boost. Overall, Dr. Mayer is a generational professor.

I enjoyed Dr. Mayer's class. He provided space to ask questions and always took the time to answer. His lecture videos were very helpful, and the homework was reasonable. The class grade was heavily based on proctored exams, but lots of recourses were provided to prepare. The content was challenging, but Dr. Mayer did a good job teaching it.

analysis.name: Tiffiny Hughes-Troutman

review_highlights.comment: I love Tiffiny. She's a bundle of joy and so sweet. She really cares about her students. Your written reflections are 40% of your grade and you only have 4, so make them count. Tests are unlimited attempts, open note. Once a week there's a surprise participation activity. Loved the lectures, exercises & rich discussions. Would definitely recommend!

She honestly felt hypocritical because this class would talk about student wellbeing and yet she did not have any grace when workload was heavy or if we requested an extension. Her lectures are fine but weren't necessarily more informative than what was in the text of the lecture slides.

Super easy, optional final. A little over half of the exam questions are copy-pasted from the end of chapter quizzes. Exams are entirely multiple choice, bit of memorization required. Study the night before using a study guide and the slides and you'll be good. She does have In-Class assignments at random for attendance, so don't skip class.

Took Troutman blindly but was pleasantly surprised by her class. Uses a point system so it's easy to keep track of your grade. One easy group project. 3 Midterms with an optional final. Has end of chapter quizzes with unlimited tries and weekly journal entries. Pretty chill class overall.
lovely professor. class mostly comprised of group discussions and in-class participation grades, with one big group project at the end. very caring.

review_highlights.comment: Professor only allows one submission to autograder per day, making it incredibly difficult to do homework. Prof. Hillegass is a caring and genuine guy. From what I've heard, the exams were a bit harder than in previous semesters, but everything ended up working out, and studying for the difficult exams is rewarded with a deeper understanding of the material. The final competition project was super fun and was an amazing way to apply what we learned.

Hillegass is the GOAT. Dude does it for the love of the game. He's a professor that actually cares about the content he teaches. Lecture is not required but I heavily recommend you go. You really don't want to miss out on them. If you genuinely put effort into learning AI for this class, you'll really come to enjoy his class, which I did.

Professor is very caring and willing to help. But the class is unexpected HARD. Other section is totally different and much easier(really). I think I prepared well for the exam and did well in the previous HARD homework, but the real one hurts me. Be ready to spend tons of hours weekly on this course if you really want to take his.

HW is already hard but the one-submission-a-day made it mad hard. Nice guy, hard course. I didn't like that all HWs and (especially) exams were completely autograded because no partial credits were awarded. At the end, there was a bonus quiz which is nice but some of the quizzes were really hard. Other sections are a lot easier.

analysis.name: Ida Yoshinaga
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very nice and lenient with students on grading & due dates. SF is her area of expertise which shows in how passionate her lectures are. Professor Yoshinaga is very knowledgeable in the sci-fi field and genre theory. She is really understanding, and is easy to contact as a student. The lectures are pretty long winded, but you don't necessarily have to pay attention to all the points she covers.

She was an amazing and enthusiastic professor! I actually enjoyed the class and would look forward to coming. The work wasn't too bad- just some presentations an a paper with some discussion posts in the mix. Overall, a great class that I'm glad I took. If you're considering animation, I'd 1000% recommend you take it with her!!

Sweetest person ever. Very accomodating to deadlines. Very few assignments, and they're pretty open ended. Cool lectures on animation, won't always be super interesting but I still enjoyed them. Had many options for extra credit. Always open to give feedback on assignments. Clearly very passionate about what she teaches, which is refreshing to see!

Ida is super sweet and definitely cares a lot about her students. Attendance is mandatory but she is pretty excited about the subject matter so the lectures are actually enjoyable to go to. However if you dont like writing, dont take the class. It is purely essays and discussion posts. Extra credit opportunities throughout the semester though

analysis.name: Mioy Huynh
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Took this class after 2 and a half years without taking chemistry. To be honest it wasn't super easy but he is an amazing prof. who you can tell not only cares about the students learning the material, but he also is really interested in what he teaches. The lab component can be annoying but he doesn't do that. Absolutely take his class if you can.

Dr. Huynh is an excellent lecturer who really cares about the class. Assignments and labs make up nearly half of your final grade, and it is very doable to get full credit on them. Exams allow cribsheets and are very doable. The final can replace midterms. The canvas course is incredibly organized and plenty of resources are available for studying.

Came into this class with very little experience with chem and was scared to take. However, the lecture notes are great, has a ton of practice problems, and has prerecorded videos on solving problems. Also you get a ton of practice exams (in addition to a ton of practice problems). A lot of material covered, but cribsheets are allowed.

Dr. Huynh is one of the most caring professors you will ever have the pleasure of meeting. CHEM 1310 is a hard course, but by attending lecture and doing the work, you will do very well. He is very accessible outside of class and he is truly a fantastic teacher. He is the type of teacher that will break down tough concepts to make them easier.

This guy is the absolute goat. His lectures were usually put in a very intuitive and direct way where what you see is what you get. Everything that is on the exams is explained somewhere in the lectures, so as long as you go to them, you'll be fine. The class definitely gets harder as it progresses, but as long as you stay locked you'll be good.

analysis.name: Itamar Kolvin
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: His lectures are hard to follow. Much of the time is spent worrying about things that do not relate to the requirements of the course. The only way to do well in physics with him as a teacher is by watching someone else's lecture videos online.

Probably the singlest worst professor/teacher i've had in my life, actively regressed my previous knowledge of physics. Never take, literally will make it seem like a 12 credit class. Principles and content that was going to be in exams was just never covered and lectures were always a week behind.

He is passionate about physics, and the class is not hard. People love to complain. How are you getting an A+ and giving him a one? I did not show up to class, but when I did, he taught as well as I expected him to. He is a good person and is passionate and cares about the material. What else can you ask for?

Awful professor. For reference, in the very second lecture we somehow went from vectors to Taylor approximations to coding, and then back to unit definitions all within the same period and presumably no link between all of the concepts. This course has been 100% self study, as his explanations are subpar at best.

Do NOT stress about your 2211 Professor!!! Course Coordinator posts all lectures online and I watched them while sitting in Kolvins class. Prioritize other things in your schedule since ur prof here doesn't matter. Clicker questions but you can get code from a friend. I wouldn't listen to his lectures cuz he goes on tangents.

analysis.name: I-Hsiang Lee
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's not a bad professor in terms of his teaching; however, this class is a lot more work than the other ISYE 3770 sections. All homeworks are written in R and they are quite time consuming. He has 2 in class "projects" that test your knowledge of how to use R. Also, the final is a decently large portion of the grade. Edit: HE CURVES THE FINAL!!

He's definitely difficult, but he makes his expectations of his students very clear. If you go to lectures and pay attention, you're good to go. He allows formula sheets on exams which is very helpful. He is very funny and personable, and he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Recommend him if you want to learn a lot.

Strikes the best balance of hilarious, engaging lectures + excellent teaching that I've seen at Tech. Lengthy homeworks requiring R but I guarantee you'll understand the material better than if you took any other instructor. Only complaint is no practice tests and difficult exams which is unfortunate, but learn the material well and you'll succeed.

Ethan is one of the best professors I've had. He cares for all his students and knows everyone's names. He really wants u to learn the material so his exams are more difficult than the other sections, but it is completely worth it. He's hilarious and u will know way more than the other sections. He makes u learn R and curves! Please take him!

He's probably one of the best GA Tech has to offer. His lectures were very engaging and entertaining. I'd say the content also isn't difficult. He's also funny, and his exam was just the homework problems but with different numbers. Final is a report, but easy.

analysis.name: Ignacio Taboada
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: I don't understand how there are several negative reviews on Dr. Taboada. His lectures are excellent and his homework is thorough.
Great professor, would take again anytime.

Taboada runs a tight ship but that is expected of quantum. He follows the textbook closely which helps because the lectures are rly dense. His grading policy is clear but also tanks alot of points with no inbetweens. HW is very hard and worth a lot in weekly problem sets but they are rly relevant. he's always available and happy to explain things!

Great lectures, the work was hard but by the end of it I could easily derive anything I did not know on tests. Super helpful with questions and test feedback outside of class, really cares about his students and wants them to succeed both in class and in the future. I got an A even though I had to work harder than most to grasp the material.

Great lecturer, explained topics thoroughly and showed where equations come from and why they work rather than just expecting you to memorize them. Tests are difficult but the homework and recitations prepare you well and he is a pretty lenient grader. He cares about his students and is happy to answer questions inside and outside of class.

one of my favorite professors i've had at tech. he cares a lot about students and is very open to making adjustments to the course based on feedback from the class. very accessible and easy to reach. things are not graded harshly and it's easy to get an A if you just put in a little bit of effort. would def take him again.

he's kinda difficult to understand and i don't think he explains the concepts well, but it was his first semester so i guess it's understandable. i will say he seems like a nice, genuine guy. i personally stopped going to class after the first couple lectures and instead watched the videos from cuyler warnock or sal barone, which i found helpful.

Dr. Ivanova is extremely knowledgable but was unapproachable and unfriendly in office hours. I really liked the head TA Will. Fun, easy, but lengthy assignments make up majority of grade.

professor ivanova was great! she's a great lecturer, and the class is really interesting. there's only two exams (midterm and final), about 11 quizzes (you can drop one), and four assignments with extra credit opportunity. all the exams/quizzes are open note, so as long as you go to/watch lecture, you'll have a very easy time in this class!

Very interesting class, and Dr. Ivanova clearly knew a lot about it! While attendance isn't mandatory and everything is posted online, weekly quizzes mean you cannot get behind in the class. This was my second time taking a class with Dr. Ingall. Highly recommend for environmental engineering majors that don't want to take ME Thermo. Grades entirely based on exams and lab work. Lab work is pretty fun, easy most of the time. Content itself is on the more interesting side imo. Get to drop lowest exam score

Thermo with Ingall is pretty easy. He is SUPER nice and knowledgeable. This is the easiest class at georgia tech, you may not learn litterally anything, but you can cram the homework the nightbefore the test and get an A.

The first 2 exams felt harder than what was covered in class. Initial rigor was high. Very new but was willing to improve. Tests were fairly difficult but test corrections and a final replacement were offered. review_highlights.comment: Normally I do not write a review as a grad student. I want to acknowledge Dr. Das for developing such a unique course in lipid biochemistry. What made the course  valuable was the incredible breadth of topics it covered. We explored lipid structures and function, lipid biochemistry and metabolism, mass spectrometry and even membrane biophysics.

Prof. Das connects course material to real-world examples. She occasionally goes on tangents, drawing on her own experiences and broader scientific topics which makes the class fun. The class required significant studying. I appreciated the open-note format, though she mentioned that future offerings may be closed to internet access.

Instructor was an expert in the subject matter and taught with a lot of enthusiasm. There was lot of opportunities to score through homework, quizzes, and open exams to promote conceptual learning. However the lectures was fast pace with occasional misalignment between lectures and exams. The FRQ portion of the exams were hard.

The class was engaging and rewarding . Dr. Das's enthusiasm and emphasis on understanding the “why” behind complex pathways helped me move beyond memorization. The course felt like a meaningful exploration of metabolism pathway and strengthened my appreciation for biochemistry as I pursue medical school.

This class prepared me for metabolism and the TCA cycle, which is great for MCAT. Real-life examples made complex ideas fun and memorable. She didn't make us memorize TCA cycle which was a big relief.  The mechanistic approach in the class and challenging ‘what if' questions pushed my thinking. Overall, I liked the class.

He sometimes made mistakes but they generally didn't affect learning. I would suggest reading the textbook before class since his lectures really help to reinforce it, and definitely do the practice exams.

Prof Hozumi is pretty good, but I would watch Prof Warnock's videos regardless of whether I attended class or not and found them a good supplement.

Lectures aren't mandatory, but I did like going to them because he writes notes by hand (even though he makes small mistakes). Class is pretty standardized, so it barely matters what professor you have. Take frequent practice tests and do the WebWorks, and you can get an A even if you don't go to class.

Prof. Hozumi can make a lot of mistakes in lecture and at times confuses himself, which can interfere with learning. For reference, I did more work (work that is also meaningless and tedious) in this class than in my grad class.

Student asks clarifying question about a provided sample for an assignment. Nagel lambasts it assuming it's the student's work. When corrected that it's in fact from her own example document, she still doesn't clarify. Of what use is this professor if she cant make a coherent assignment or even realize shes critiquing her own example as inadequate?

Every week, 150 precious minutes of my life are ripped away in the most agonizing fashion. Her lectures, where are often devices banned, feels like enduring purgatory. I wonder what I could accomplish with that time. Maybe I could cure cancer or rediscover joy. I'll never know, thanks to this painfully redundant and utterly uninspiring class.
